title: Mixed join subset and its relative index-simplex attachments
statement: Use small simplicial sets and simplicial subsets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], ordinary nerves and standard simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the explicit ordered-join construction of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. Write $\partial\Delta^n$ for the simplicial subset of $\Delta^n$ consisting in degree $m$ of the nonsurjective monotone maps $[m]\to[n]$. A pushout square means that maps from its lower-right object to any simplicial set are uniquely specified by maps from the other two adjacent objects agreeing on the upper-left object. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, let $I$ be any small partially ordered set, and let $K_i\subseteq K$ be simplicial subsets with $K_i\subseteq K_j$ for $i\leq j$. Define a degreewise subset $H\subseteq K\star N(I)$ by including both pure factors and exactly the mixed simplices $\sigma\star(i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_r)$ for which $\sigma\in K_{i_0}$. This is a simplicial subset. For any simplicial subset $Y\subseteq N(I)$, let $H_Y\subseteq H$ contain all of $K$, the pure simplices of $Y$, and precisely the mixed simplices whose final block belongs to $Y$. Then $H_\varnothing=K$, $H_{N(I)}=H$, and $H_{\bigcup_\alpha Y_\alpha}=K\cup\bigcup_\alpha H_{Y_\alpha}$ for every increasing family $(Y_\alpha)$ (including the empty family); for a nonempty family the extra union with $K$ is redundant. Suppose $Y'$ is obtained from $Y$ by adjoining a single nondegenerate $n$-simplex $\tau=(i_0<\cdots<i_n)$ not already in $Y$ and whose entire boundary belongs to $Y$. The commutative square with horizontal arrows $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n\to H_Y$ and $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n\to H_{Y'}$, and vertical inclusions $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n$ and $H_Y\hookrightarrow H_{Y'}$, is a pushout of simplicial sets. The lower map concatenates a simplex of $K_{i_0}$ with a face or degeneracy of $\tau$, and uses the pure-factor inclusions on the pure summands. Here $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, so the vertex case attaches $K_i^{\triangleright}=K_i\star\Delta^0$ along $K_i$. Neither directedness, a covering hypothesis, nor nonemptiness of $I$, $K$ or any $K_i$ is assumed.

source.place: HTT Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2 and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp. 248-250: the square for an index-simplex attachment, specialized to inclusions indexed by a poset. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial/quasicategorical comparison.

proof.text: Use the disjoint pure and mixed summands in the ordered-join formula of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. An operator on a mixed simplex either leaves only one block, hence gives a permitted pure simplex, or restricts both blocks. In the latter case its new initial index is some $i_j\geq i_0$, and its new first block is an operator applied to $\sigma\in K_{i_0}$, so belongs to $K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_j}$. Operators on pure factors remain pure. This verifies closure for every monotone operator, hence the degreewise subset $H$ is a simplicial subset in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1 and Remark 4.2.3.2, printed pp. 248-249: restriction of the two ordered blocks. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: Fix a simplicial subset $Y\subseteq N(I)$. An operator on a mixed simplex of $H_Y$ that retains both blocks sends its final block into $Y$, because $Y$ is a simplicial subset. If only the final block survives, the result is a pure simplex of $Y$; if only the initial block survives, the result lies in $K$. Pure $Y$ and pure $K$ simplices are also preserved. Thus $H_Y$ is a simplicial subset of $H$. In particular $Y\subseteq Z$ implies $H_Y\subseteq H_Z$ by the membership rule.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 249: the subsets denoted K_X. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: No pure nerve or mixed simplex has final block in the empty simplicial subset, so $H_\varnothing=K$; allowing every final block gives $H_{N(I)}=H$. For any increasing family $(Y_\alpha)$, a pure nerve or mixed simplex belongs to $H_{\bigcup_\alpha Y_\alpha}$ exactly when its final block lies in some $Y_\alpha$, exactly when it belongs to some $H_{Y_\alpha}$. All pure $K$ simplices occur on the left regardless of the family. This proves $H_{\bigcup_\alpha Y_\alpha}=K\cup\bigcup_\alpha H_{Y_\alpha}$, including the empty family. For a nonempty family each $H_{Y_\alpha}$ already contains $K$, giving the original union formula in that case.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp. 249-250: initial, terminal and nonzero limit stages. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: Write $t:\Delta^n\to N(I)$ for $t(f)=(i_{f(0)}\leq\cdots\leq i_{f(b)})$ on an arbitrary $f:[b]\to[n]$. The strict inequalities among the $i_j$ imply that $t(f)$ determines $f$, so $t$ is degreewise injective. If $f$ is nonsurjective, it belongs to $\partial\Delta^n$ and $t(f)\in Y$ by the boundary hypothesis. If $f$ is surjective, choose its monotone section $s:[n]\to[b]$ by taking the least element of each fiber. Then $t(f)\in Y$ would imply $\tau=s^*t(f)\in Y$, a contradiction. Consequently $t^{-1}(Y)=\partial\Delta^n$ in every degree. This also holds for $n=0$: every $[b]\to[0]$ is surjective.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 250: adjoining a nondegenerate index simplex; boundary inverse image made explicit. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: Put $A=K_{i_0}$, $B=A\star\Delta^n$, and $C=A\star\partial\Delta^n$. Define $u:B\to H_{Y\prime}$ by the pure inclusion of $A$ into $K$, by $t$ on the pure simplex factor, and by $(\sigma,f)\mapsto\sigma\star t(f)$ on a mixed summand. This mixed simplex lies in $H$: its first index is $i_{f(0)}\geq i_0$, and $\sigma\in K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_{f(0)}}$. Its final block is in $Y\prime$. The formulas commute with each operator by restriction of the blocks, including an empty block. They define a simplicial map. This map is injective in each degree because it preserves the summand and both coordinates, $A\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, and $t$ is injective.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 250: the lower map from K_{I_0} star sigma. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: Compute the inverse image $u^{-1}(H_Y)$. Every pure $A$ simplex is in it and in $C$. A pure $\Delta^n$ simplex $f$ is in it precisely when $t(f)\in Y$, hence precisely when $f\in\partial\Delta^n$ by step 4. The same equivalence holds for a mixed simplex $(\sigma,f)$, since membership in $H_Y$ tests exactly its final block. Thus $u^{-1}(H_Y)=C$. In particular $u|_C$ lands in $H_Y$, giving the upper horizontal arrow and making the stated square commute. Both vertical arrows are inclusions of simplicial subsets.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 250: the overlap of the index-simplex attachment. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: By adjoining $\tau$ we mean $Y\prime=Y\cup t(\Delta^n)$, the union of simplicial subsets. A simplex of $H_{Y\prime}$ outside $H_Y$ is not pure $K$. Its nonempty final block must therefore be $t(f)$ for some $f:[b]\to[n]$, and $f$ must be surjective by step 4. For a pure nerve simplex this is already in $u(B)$. For a mixed simplex its first index is $i_{f(0)}=i_0$, so its first block lies in $K_{i_0}=A$, and it too belongs to $u(B)$. Consequently $H_{Y\prime}=H_Y\cup u(B)$ degreewise; step 6 identifies the intersection as $u(C)$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 250: every new simplex is in the displayed join cell. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: To verify the pushout without invoking a colimit theorem, let $T$ be any simplicial set and let $g:H_Y\to T$, $h:B\to T$ agree after restriction to $C$. Define a function in each degree on $H_{Y\prime}=H_Y\cup u(B)$ by $g(x)$ on $H_Y$ and $h(b)$ on $u(b)$. Injectivity of $u$ and the equality $H_Y\cap u(B)=u(C)$ make it well-defined. For any simplicial operator, represent its input in $H_Y$ or in $u(B)$; that same representative gives its image under the operator, and naturality follows from naturality of $g$ or $h$. Agreement on the overlap handles either representation. Thus these functions give a simplicial map, and coverage by the two images proves its uniqueness. This is exactly the pushout universal property specified in the statement.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 250: universal property of its pushout square, expanded degreewise. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.

proof.text: For $n=0$, the boundary has no simplices, so the join formula gives $A\star\partial\Delta^0=A$ and $A\star\Delta^0=A^{\triangleright}$. The same square therefore attaches the local cone along $A$. If $A=\varnothing$, this attaches just the pure vertex. If $K=\varnothing$, all mixed summands vanish and the square is the usual boundary attachment in $N(I)$. If $I=\varnothing$, then $H=H_\varnothing=K$ and no index-simplex attachment is possible. Every construction and calculation above uses only the given inclusions and monotonicity, never directedness, a covering condition, or nonemptiness.

source.place: Remark 4.2.3.2 and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp. 249-250: vertex attachments and empty-factor conventions. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Elementary agent expansion of the poset-inclusion case.
